title: Modification of comet-FISH technique by using temperature instead of chemical denaturation
author: Mladinic, Zeljezic

steps.title: Clean and coat slides
steps.instruction: Ensure microscope slides are grease‑free; if needed soak in alcohol, wipe dry, then immerse each slide in a Coplin jar containing melted 1 % NMP agarose, wipe the back, drain excess agarose and air‑dry the slides overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 % LMP agarose
steps.instruction: Heat 0.5 % low‑melting‑point (LMP) agarose in a microwave, transfer to a water bath set at 37 °C and allow it to equilibrate to this temperature.

steps.title: Isolate lymphocytes
steps.instruction: Mix whole blood with Histopaque® 1077 at a 1:1 (v/v) ratio, centrifuge 30 min at 400 × g, collect the buffy‑coat layer with a Pasteur pipette, resuspend cells in PBS or RPMI‑1640 medium to a total volume of 5 ml, centrifuge 5 min at 250 × g, discard supernatant, add PBS or RPMI to a final volume of 1 ml and resuspend the cells.

steps.title: Mix cells with agarose
steps.instruction: Aliquot 1–10 µl of the cell suspension into a microcentrifuge tube, add 100 µl of the warmed 0.5 % LMP agarose, and mix by aspirating the mixture up and down with a pipette.

steps.title: Apply cell‑agarose to slides
steps.instruction: Place 100 µl of the cell‑agarose mixture onto the precoated slide, use the same pipette tip, cover with a 24 × 40 mm coverslip, and keep the slide on ice for 5–10 min until the agarose polymerizes.

steps.title: Equilibrate slides in SSC
steps.instruction: Immerse the air‑dried comet slides in 2× SSC solution in a Coplin jar for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Dehydrate slides through ethanol
steps.instruction: Wash the slides sequentially in 70 %, 96 % and 100 % ethanol for 5 min each, using a Coplin jar.

steps.title: Prewarm slide and probe
steps.instruction: Place both the slide and the FISH probe in a 37 °C environment for 5 min to prewarm them.

steps.title: Apply probe and coverslip
steps.instruction: Pipette 10 µl of the warmed probe onto the selected area of the slide, carefully place an 18 mm × 18 mm coverslip over it.

description: Comet-FISH technique is an extension of commonly used comet assay. Its purpose is to determine whether primary damage which comet assay detects, affected specific gene (or other sequence) of interest [1]. Signal detected in the tail of the comet indicates damage to the DNA sequence of interest. In short, comet-FISH technique consists of the following steps: (a) preparation of the comet assay slides; (b) performing the lysis, denaturation and electrophoresis; (c) performing fluorescent in situ hybridization on comet assay slides; (d) analysis of slides (evaluation of primary DNA damage and/or specific gene damage). In preparation of comet assay slides we used leukocytes from whole blood and isolated lymphocytes.
